data.description:
## Context / Problem

The ingestion operation [rebar:INGEST] only removes the manual sweep if something runs it on a schedule with the credentials it needs: read access to CloudWatch alarm history and to this repository's Actions runs, plus write access to the `tickets` branch. This repository already runs scheduled filers with exactly that shape — `reconcile-bridge-canary.yml` (tickets worktree mount at lines 99-105, signing-key materialisation at 133-151, `contents: write` at 66) and `terraform-drift.yml` (OIDC `id-token: write`, `aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v6` assuming `arn:aws:iam::896586841071:role/rebar-terraform-plan`, lines 25-42) — so the cron is a composition of proven steps, not a new mechanism class.

## Approach

- **Workflow** `.github/workflows/ops-alert-ingest.yml`: `schedule: '27 * * * *'` (hourly; CloudWatch retains 30 days of alarm history, so a missed hour is re-read, never lost) plus `workflow_dispatch` with a `dry_run` boolean input. Steps mirror the canary: checkout with full history, mount the `tickets` worktree, install rebar from the checkout, materialise the bot signing key, assume the AWS role via OIDC, then `rebar alerts ingest --source cloudwatch` and `rebar alerts ingest --source github-actions` (the latter authenticated by `GITHUB_TOKEN` with `actions: read`). `concurrency: {group: ops-alert-ingest, cancel-in-progress: false}` so overlapping hours serialise. Permissions are the minimum union: `contents: write`, `id-token: write`, `actions: read`.
- **IAM** (Terraform, `infra/terraform/iam_alert_ingest.tf`): a new role `rebar-alert-ingest` federated to this repository through the existing OIDC provider (`infra/terraform/oidc.tf`), trust policy scoped to `repo:navapbc/rebar:ref:refs/heads/main` exactly as `rebar-terraform-plan` is, with an inline policy of two read actions only — `cloudwatch:DescribeAlarmHistory`, `cloudwatch:DescribeAlarms` — resource-scoped to `arn:aws:cloudwatch:us-east-1:896586841071:alarm:rebar-*`. No wildcard, no write actions (the single-action precedent is `infra/terraform/iam_bridge_metrics.tf:27-40`). State stays in the existing remote S3 backend; the apply is operator-run per `docs/gerrit-aws-setup.md`.
- **Staged rollout** (ADR 0114 advisory-first): the workflow lands with env `INGEST_DRY_RUN: "true"`, so scheduled runs post `INGEST … (dry-run)` ledger comments and file nothing. After the operator reads at least three consecutive clean dry-run ledger reports, a separate one-line change flips it to `"false"`. Rollback is flipping it back or disabling the workflow in the Actions UI — no data cleanup, because the ingester's writes are ordinary tickets.
- **Out-of-loop proof** (T15): before the schedule fires for real, the operator triggers `workflow_dispatch` with `dry_run: true` once and records the run id and report on this ticket; the live local dry-run recorded on the ingestion child is the proof of the operation itself.

Positive rationale: reusing the canary's tickets-worktree and signing steps and the drift workflow's OIDC pattern keeps every credential path one already reviewed; a read-only two-action role is the smallest grant that lets the operation see alarm history; hourly polling matches the signal's own resolution (alarm periods are minutes, sweeps were daily).

Failure disposition: a failed run is itself surfaced by the next run's ledger comment showing an unmoved watermark (the ingester never advances it on error) — transient; the workflow's own red run is visible in Actions but is deliberately **not** in the ingester's allowlist to avoid self-filing.

## Scope

- `.github/workflows/ops-alert-ingest.yml` (new).
- `infra/terraform/iam_alert_ingest.tf` (new), `infra/terraform/oidc.tf` (subject list if the provider's condition enumerates workflows), `docs/gerrit-aws-setup.md` (role table), `infra/runbooks/ops-alert-ingest.md` (new: dispatch, dry-run flip, disabling).
- `scripts/check_verify_gate_parity.py` waiver list only if the parity gate enumerates scheduled workflows (the existing scheduled canaries establish the precedent to follow).
- `tests/unit/test_workflow_ops_alert_ingest.py` (new: YAML contract test).

## Testing

- Workflow YAML contract test (the repository's existing pattern for pinning workflow shape): the file parses; permissions are exactly `{contents: write, id-token: write, actions: read}`; `concurrency.cancel-in-progress` is false; both `rebar alerts ingest` invocations are present; `INGEST_DRY_RUN` defaults to `"true"`; the schedule is hourly.
- Terraform: `terraform validate` and `terraform plan` in the drift workflow stay green; a unit test over the rendered policy JSON asserts the action set is exactly the two read actions and the resource is the `rebar-*` alarm ARN pattern.
- CI-trigger audit (T14): the new schedule affects no other workflow's trigger filter; the workflow itself is `NO_FILTER` on refs (schedule + dispatch only). Gate: `make test`, `terraform-drift.yml`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `.github/workflows/ops-alert-ingest.yml` exists with the hourly schedule, the `dry_run` dispatch input, the minimum permission set, and `INGEST_DRY_RUN: "true"`; verified by `tests/unit/test_workflow_ops_alert_ingest.py`.
- [ ] The `rebar-alert-ingest` role grants exactly `cloudwatch:DescribeAlarmHistory` and `cloudwatch:DescribeAlarms` on `alarm:rebar-*` and nothing else; verified by the policy-JSON unit test and `terraform validate`.
- [ ] [non-codebase] The role is applied: the operator records the role ARN and the `terraform apply` timestamp as a comment on this ticket.
- [ ] [non-codebase] One `workflow_dispatch` run with `dry_run: true` completes green and its ledger report (window, counts, zero writes) is recorded as a comment on this ticket with the run id.
- [ ] [non-codebase] Three consecutive scheduled dry-run ledger reports are clean (no source errors, watermark advancing) before the flip change is pushed; the operator records the three run ids on this ticket.
- [ ] `infra/runbooks/ops-alert-ingest.md` documents dispatch, the dry-run flip, and how to disable the schedule; verified by the docs-drift gate.
data.title: Scheduled alert ingestion: hourly GitHub Actions cron, read-only rebar-alert-ingest OIDC role, dry-run-first rollout
